description: Four signals measured against a voltage captured earlier, in 2HP, reporting how far each has moved since

params.text: Captures the present input voltages as the new references, for one cycle per press in trigger mode or for as long as it is held in gate mode
Switches the reset control between red for a trigger, which captures once however long the signal stays high, and green for a gate, which keeps capturing while it is high
Chooses which references are used: Ind gives every section its own, A-only measures all four against the A section's references
Steps the outputs through Sg for the plain difference, In for the difference multiplied by -1, and Ab for the difference without its sign

inputs.text: A rising edge, or a high gate in gate mode, captures the present input voltages as the new references
One of the four signals being measured

outputs.text: Carries how far that input has moved from its reference, in the form the output mode sets

notes: the captured references are saved with the patch and are not disturbed by unplugging an input, so a reference taken from one module can be used to measure another
in gate mode, while the reset is held every output reads 0V, since the references are being taken again on every cycle
in A-only mode the A output itself reads 0V, because A is being measured against its own reference; this is how the module strips a moving DC offset off B, C and D
menu: Update A-D reference values — sets the stored references of all four sections to a named voltage
Update A reference values, Update B reference values, Update C reference values, Update D reference values — sets that one section's stored references to a named voltage
Clipping range — clamps every output to the range chosen, -12V to 12V unless you change it, and Off lets the output run to any voltage
Process quality: Audio, High, Balanced, Low, Very low — sets how often the module runs its algorithm, from every cycle down to every 256th; below Balanced a 1ms trigger can be missed
Gate-high detect-level — sets the voltage at which an incoming gate counts as high, 1V or more unless you change it
Trigger-high detect-level — sets the voltage at which an incoming trigger counts as high, 1V or more unless you change it
Trigger-low detect-level — sets the voltage an incoming trigger must fall back below before the next one is counted, under 0.1V unless you change it

inputs.0:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
